The issue is fixed. Summary of changes:

**`gson/src/main/java/com/google/gson/internal/bind/TypeAdapters.java`** — the built-in primitive adapters (`BYTE`, `SHORT`, `INTEGER`, `LONG`, `FLOAT`, `DOUBLE`) now perform numeric conversion when writing, using the primitive `JsonWriter.value(...)` overloads instead of `JsonWriter.value(Number)` (which just emitted `Number.toString()`):
- `BYTE` → `out.value((long) value.byteValue())`
- `SHORT` → `out.value((long) value.shortValue())`
- `INTEGER` → `out.value((long) value.intValue())`
- `LONG` → `out.value(value.longValue())`
- `FLOAT` → `out.value(value.floatValue())`
- `DOUBLE` → `out.value(value.doubleValue())`
- Each handles `null` with `out.nullValue()` (previously implicit via `value(Number)`).

**`gson/src/main/java/com/google/gson/Gson.java`** — the default `doubleAdapter`/`floatAdapter` variants used for regular (non-special-FP) Gson instances were bypassing the conversion; they now write `out.value(doubleValue)` / `out.value(floatValue)`.

Verification:
- `new Gson().toJson(1.5, byte.class)` now emits `1` (narrowing conversion), and widening cases like `toJson(1L, double.class)` emit `1.0`.
- `PrimitiveTest` (108 tests, including the conversion expectations like `toJson(128, Byte.class) == "-128"`) passes; the full `gson` module suite passes except `TypeHierarchyAdapterTest.testTypeHierarchy`, which I confirmed also fails on the unmodified tree (pre-existing, unrelated).
